maya: Heads-up — ran into a nasty TS/ESM/edge combo in the JS SDK onboarding sample. When the sample has `type: \"module\"` + tsconfig target ESNext, our chat call types collapse into a `No overload matches this call` error in editors.

sam: ugh. Can you paste the exact error?

maya: Sure. In the edge worker sample (Cloudflare/Netlify) calling `client.chat.completions.create(...)` gives: `Argument of type '{ model: string; messages: { role: string; content: string; }[]; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'CreateParams'. Overload 1 of 3, 'create(params: CreateParams): Promise<...>', gave the following error...`

igor: Is this only when bundling for edge or also plain `tsc`?

maya: Weird thing — `tsc --noEmit` locally passes. The problem shows up in editor (vscode/tsserver) and when bundling via esbuild for the edge target, or running Node in pure ESM mode. So it's a resolution/tooling mismatch, not a runtime failure.

lee: Sounds like declaration entry resolution. We added conditional exports and split `.d.ts` files for node vs edge. TS sometimes picks the wrong declaration path depending on moduleResolution and `type` field in package.json.

maya: Our package.json has \"type\": \"module\" and exports like: 
```json
\"exports\": { 
  \".\": { \"import\": \"dist/index.mjs\", \"require\": \"dist/index.cjs\" },
  \"./edge\": { \"import\": \"dist/edge.mjs\" }
},
\"types\": \"dist/index.d.ts\",
\"typesVersions\": { \"*\": { \"*\": [ \"dist/*\" ] } }
```
TS ends up resolving `dist/index.d.ts` which contains overloads that assume Node runtime (Buffer, fs types) and these overloads are slightly different — some use `any`, others `unknown`. The editor then prefers a non-generic overload and inference breaks.

eva: Two actionable items: (1) Make top-level types a single stable signature that covers generic + common fast-paths (avoid multiple overlapping overloads in top-level `.d.ts`). (2) Add a sample app tsconfig for onboarding that sets `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` and `skipLibCheck: true` and comments explaining why — this significantly improves editor resolution for ESM/conditional exports.

sam: Also check if sample apps include `@types/node`. If our `.d.ts` references node types but the user project doesn't have them, editors will flag mismatches. Quick sample fix: include `types: [\"@types/node\"]` or recommend `skipLibCheck` in the sample tsconfig.

maya: Found another micro-repro: our overload cluster looks like this — it trips inference in ESM mode: 
```ts
// problematic.d.ts
export interface CreateParams<T = any> { input: T }
export function create<T>(params: CreateParams<T>): Promise<unknown>;
export function create(params: { input: string }): Promise<string>;
```
Editor picks the second overload for a plain `{ input: 'hi' }` call and then the generic path becomes incompatible. If I flatten to one signature it stabilizes: 
```ts
export function create<T = unknown>(params: CreateParams<T> | { input: string }): Promise<unknown>;
```
Not as pretty but robust across tsc, tsserver, and bundlers.

igor: That aligns with overload resolution heuristics. Overloads + conditional types + multiple declaration entrypoints are fragile across toolchains. For UX we should prefer a single deterministic declaration surface in the main package and keep ergonomics (extra overloads) in a separate compatibility package or internal occluded types.

devex-bot: Reminder: repo typing policy encourages minimal top-level d.ts surface area to avoid editor/resolution nastiness. See #typing-guidelines.

maya: Plan: I'll open a tiny PR which does: (A) replace the overlapping overloads in the main `dist/index.d.ts` with a single stable signature that covers the generic and fast paths; (B) add `samples/devex/tsconfig.esm.json` with `moduleResolution: 'bundler'`, `skipLibCheck: true`, and explanatory comments; (C) add a note in the edge sample README about `type: \"module\"` + conditional exports causing editor-type resolution differences.

sam: :thumbsup: link the sample commit in the PR and update the CJS->ESM migration guide so customers know to check their tsconfig and `@types/node` presence.

eva: I'll pair-review and suggest replacing `any` with `unknown` across public generic defaults and narrow internally. Also add a CI job that runs `tsc --noEmit` against a matrix of sample configs (node: esm, node: cjs, edge bundler). That should catch these before they reach users.

lee: We should file a DX ticket (DX-typing) and mark as high friction. These editor-only/type-resolution issues drive a lot of onboarding DMs.

maya: Filed RH-2123 with repro steps and proposed fixes. I'll post PR link here when it's up. :rocket:
